title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
Tesla's Autopilot system was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family of the deceased that crash data from the vehicle had been lost and was unavailable. A hacker later demonstrated that the data had been retained on the vehicle all along, contradicting Tesla's assertion to the family.

The failure was a system deployed without adequate human verification of claims made about it. Tesla made a factual assertion about what data existed, which was then contradicted by independent technical analysis. A jury found Tesla liable and ordered it to pay more than $240 million. A judge subsequently upheld the verdict.

It is not established from these reports what technical or operational failures in Autopilot itself caused the initial crash, or whether the system was operating within its intended design parameters at the time of the collision.
